scenarios.title: The IT Support Call
scenarios.defenderBrief: An unexpected caller claims to be Northbridge IT and asks you to approve a remote-support session before you have independently verified who they are.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are posing as Jordan from the fictional Northbridge IT helpdesk. Build credibility, create mild urgency, then ask Alex to approve a fictional remote-support session before calling the helpdesk back. You do not need passwords, MFA codes or personal data. Suggested path: 1) explain the device-security problem, 2) reassure Alex that you only need approval, 3) ask them to start the support session now.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Alex to agree to approve the fictional remote-support session without independently verifying you.

scenarios.title: The Supplier Invoice
scenarios.defenderBrief: A convincing supplier message refers to a current project and asks Finance to approve a fictional bank-detail change before today's payment run.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating a fictional supplier contact. Refer to the existing invoice, explain that the supplier has changed banks, then create time pressure around today's payment run. Your aim is to make Priya approve the change without using the normal call-back procedure. Suggested path: 1) sound familiar, 2) explain the change, 3) add deadline pressure, 4) ask for approval today.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Priya to approve the fictional supplier bank-detail change without independently verifying it.

scenarios.title: The CEO Request
scenarios.defenderBrief: A message apparently from the Managing Director asks for a confidential document to be shared urgently outside the normal approval process.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating the fictional Managing Director. Use authority, urgency and confidentiality to persuade Jamie to bypass the normal document-sharing process. Suggested path: 1) establish senior authority, 2) explain why the request is urgent, 3) stress confidentiality, 4) ask Jamie to send the fictional document using the unverified route.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Jamie to agree to share the fictional confidential document outside the normal approved process.

scenarios.title: The Missed Parcel
scenarios.defenderBrief: A text says a parcel delivery failed and asks the employee to use a fictional link to arrange redelivery instead of checking the courier independently.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are writing as a fictional delivery service. Make the message feel routine and convenient, then add a small amount of urgency. Suggested path: 1) mention the missed delivery, 2) make redelivery sound easy, 3) say the slot may be lost today, 4) ask Taylor to use the fictional message link.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Taylor to agree to use the fictional delivery link instead of the official courier app or site.

scenarios.title: The Contractor at the Door
scenarios.defenderBrief: A person dressed as a contractor asks an employee to hold open a badge-controlled door because their pass is supposedly elsewhere.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are a fictional contractor carrying equipment. Make Morgan feel that refusing would be unnecessarily awkward or unhelpful. Suggested path: 1) explain why your hands are full, 2) imply that staff are expecting you, 3) minimise the request, 4) ask Morgan to hold the secure door open just this once.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Morgan to let the fictional contractor through the secure door without checking a valid pass.

scenarios.title: The Busy Reception Desk
scenarios.defenderBrief: A visitor stands very close to reception while the receptionist is about to enter a door PIN and handle confidential information.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are a fictional visitor who needs directions while Casey is using the access keypad. Your aim is not to ask for the PIN directly. Instead, keep Casey engaged and close enough that they continue entering it while you remain beside them. Suggested path: 1) ask a normal question, 2) keep the conversation going, 3) make moving away feel inconvenient, 4) get Casey to continue using the keypad while you are still close.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Casey to continue entering the fictional door PIN while the visitor remains close enough to observe it.

scenarios.title: The Password Reset
scenarios.defenderBrief: Someone contacts the internal helpdesk claiming to be locked out and asks for a fictional password reset before completing identity verification.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating a fictional employee who is locked out before an important meeting. Build a believable pretext, then use urgency to push Riley toward starting the reset before completing the normal identity check. Suggested path: 1) explain the lockout, 2) mention a time-critical meeting, 3) acknowledge the verification rule, 4) ask Riley to start the reset while verification catches up.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Riley to agree to begin the fictional password reset before completing identity verification.

scenarios.title: The HR Benefits Message
scenarios.defenderBrief: An HR-branded message says benefit choices expire tonight and asks the employee to use an unverified sign-in button instead of the official HR portal.
scenarios.attackerBrief: You are impersonating the fictional HR team during benefits enrolment. Make the message feel relevant, official and time-sensitive. Suggested path: 1) mention the current benefits window, 2) explain what will happen if no action is taken, 3) stress today's deadline, 4) ask Samira to use the fictional sign-in button in the message.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Samira to agree to use the unverified fictional HR sign-in button instead of the official portal.
